new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the first syllable of disyllabic words (monosyllables are stressed). The source says nothing about words of three or more syllables, so 'initial' is established only for disyllables; no weight conditioning is mentioned (examples include a light initial syllable gɪ.t͡ʃi and heavy-initial t̪ʊm.ɖi, both initial-stressed).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement based on isolated citation forms; no discussion of phrase-level prosody. The companion phonemic summary (Kumar 2015, p. 44) explicitly states stress and intonation were not investigated, so the 2017 statement is a brief impressionistic addition, not an analysed stress study.
new_statements.identity_note: Both saved documents describe the Patalkot valley variety of Bhariati (Chhindwara District, Madhya Pradesh; language resource persons from Rather village), which the authors say is the dialect accepted as most intelligible by speakers of the Tamia/Harrai/Jamai block dialects. This is glottocode bhar1241 / ISO bha itself (no sub-dialect glottocodes exist). Note the our source list lat/lon (22.34 N, 83.11 E) lies in Chhattisgarh, well east of Patalkot (approx. 22.4 N, 78.7 E); the language is Indo-Aryan (Bundeli-like) despite Ethnologue's older Dravidian classification, as both Grierson 1906 and Kumar 2015 state.

In disyllabic words the first syllable is stressed.' with examples gɪ.t͡ʃi 'neck', t̪ɐɾ.ʋa 'foot', t̪ʊm.ɖi 'bottle gourd'. Nothing said about words of three or more syllables, secondary stress, or weight.
